correctness.rationale: For subcritical alpha, choose an intermediate alpha_0 so that sigma_0=1-alpha_0 lies in the strict compactness interval of arXiv:2610.00292v1 Theorem 6.1; compact resolvent gives D(B) compactly embedded in H and the Hilbert interpolation identity identifies the target with D(B^{alpha_0}). Critical boundedness is exactly Theorem 7.2. For an arbitrary fixed compact-resolvent B, normalized eigenmodes beta_n^{-1} exp(i beta_n^{1/m} t)e_n have uniformly bounded graph norm, critical images separated by the constant sqrt(2) T^{(1-lambda)/p}, and supercritical image norms growing like beta_n^{alpha-(1-j/m)}. This proves all quantifiers and all three regimes without experimental inference.

value.rationale: The exponent 1-j/m is the focal source's natural sharp Hilbert regularity level. Determining whether compactness survives at that exact level is a structural question left open by a theorem stated only after strict interpolation loss. The fixed-operator classification shows that the loss is genuinely necessary for every infinite-dimensional compact-resolvent Hilbert scale, not merely for one counterexample, while also identifying the full supercritical unbounded regime. This closes a natural boundary rather than adding an arbitrary parameter slice.
